keyFindings.claim: Readability comes from value, not hue; a frame must survive a grayscale/squint test with 3-4 grouped value masses and the subject on a contrasting mass.
keyFindings.detail: Desaturate the frame and check the shapes still separate. A strong frame squints down to a 3-value notan with one dominant band (about 45-65%) and a small accent band.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Measured on the cave battle: the notan splits 35/45/20 with no dominant band. In the squint image the brightest mass is the window and beams, not the creatures.

keyFindings.claim: The focal point must hold the frame's highest local contrast (value, saturation, temperature, detail) while the rest stays restrained.
keyFindings.detail: Standard painting and art-direction rule. It can be measured as the ratio of local L*-std, chroma and edge energy inside the focal box versus a surrounding ring.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Cave focal vs ring: L-std 19.2 vs 18.5, chroma 35 vs 34, edges 6.5 vs 5.3. Meadow: edges 9.5 vs 9.6, and chroma is lower at the focus. Creatures do not win the frame.

keyFindings.claim: Detail density should be a gradient (high near focus/gameplay, low at edges and in big planes); uniform noise everywhere reads as amateur/procedural.
keyFindings.detail: Negative space and rest areas let key elements breathe (e.g. Dark Souls bonfires). Measured as the coefficient of variation of gradient energy over a 6x8 grid.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Meadow detail CV is 0.195, almost uniform. paintRock/paintBoulder apply the same fbm+chips+cracks to every face. Detail should be modulated by light and by distance from focus.

keyFindings.claim: Palettes should be built from hue-shifted ramps with saturation peaking mid-ramp, drawn from a limited per-scene gamut, with accents reserved for subjects.
keyFindings.detail: Slynyrd: straight ramps look flat; bright+saturated burns the eyes; dark+saturated looks heavy. Gurney's gamut mask preselects a palette region on the colour wheel.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: The RAMPS already hue-shift, but no gamut is reserved. In the cave, 99% of chromatic pixels fall in two orange/yellow 30-degree bins, so the flame kin has no free hue to pop against.

keyFindings.claim: Temperature contrast between key light and shadow is a primary lighting tool; same-hue lights and shadows read as a filter.
keyFindings.detail: Warm key with cool or plum shadows, or a cool key with warm bounce. Measurable as the mean b* in shadows versus lights.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Cave shadows have b* +18.5 vs lights +31.6, i.e. still orange despite the plum split-tone grade. The summit night arena (-10.7 vs +13.3) shows the split working. Push cool shadow colour in warm arenas.

keyFindings.claim: In games, use rim/background light to silhouette subjects; keep one dominant, motivated key direction.
keyFindings.detail: Shaver (GDC 2018 Invisible Intuition): three-point lighting breaks with free cameras, so use rim and background lights in encounters. The Last of Us lighting talk: dominant directionality, ambient shadows, bounce.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: The battle camera is fixed per layout, so a real rim light per kin is possible. Raise SpriteLight.rim for warm-on-warm pairings.

keyFindings.claim: HD-2D = pixel sprites in a 3D diorama, dramatic light/shadow interacting with pixel surfaces, tilt-shift DoF, selective bloom, extra point lights for FX.
keyFindings.detail: Developer statements via Unreal spotlights and Wikipedia. A fan reimplementation spec gives FOV 25-35 deg, pitch 35-45 deg, 32/48-texel tiles, characters about 1.5 tiles, nearest filtering, and a single directional light with sprite shadows.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Orbkin's pipeline already matches the technical recipe. The remaining gap is art direction (value grouping, gamut, focal contrast, UI), not missing tech.

keyFindings.claim: God rays and atmosphere must be used sparingly and must not cover the subject; atmospheric perspective lowers contrast/saturation with distance and converges to the fog/sky value.
keyFindings.detail: Aerial perspective: contrast and saturation fall and hue shifts toward the background colour. Shafts should land beside the action and have a visible source.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: The cave shafts cross the player's side and are the brightest mass in the squint image. Cut to 2-3 shafts and cap their added light on the kin region.

keyFindings.claim: VFX readability: a primary element (high value range, opaque, strong shape, intense motion) plus subdued secondaries; visual weight equals gameplay weight; anticipation-climax-dissipation timing kept short.
keyFindings.detail: League of Legends VFX Style Guide (Riot, 2017): five areas (gameplay, value, colour, shape, timing).
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Audit movefx so each move has one primary opaque shape and is scaled to its power.

keyFindings.claim: UI must belong to the world's art direction (palette, typography, frame motif); style mismatch is a top immersion breaker.
keyFindings.detail: For pixel JRPG battles: nine-slice frames at the world texel scale, a cream/ink palette with one accent, a pixel typeface, and colour reserved for state.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: The candy-saturated pink/orange/green/violet buttons and the modern sans font are the most saturated things on screen and outrank the creatures. Re-skin as a cheap, high-impact fix.

keyFindings.claim: Silhouette-first creature design: black-fill test at thumbnail size, a lineup test across the cast, shape semantics (round = friendly, square = sturdy, spiky/diagonal = danger), evolutions change silhouette not scale.
keyFindings.detail: The three-read hierarchy: silhouette at 32 px, colour blocks at 64 px, then detail.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Every Orbkin species uses the same ellipsoid+cone+cylinder vocabulary. Give each line a shape motif and add an automated silhouette solidity/IoU test.

keyFindings.claim: Pixel consistency: one texel/pixel density everywhere; mixels (mixed pixel sizes, rotated or scaled sprites) read as amateur.
keyFindings.detail: Keep the scale at 1 with a base viewport; mixed asset packs break consistency.
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Orbkin already enforces TEXEL=1/16 and integer upscales. Keep that invariant for any new Blender-baked or imported assets, and for the UI frames.

keyFindings.claim: Automated pixel metrics (notan shares, b* split, hue dominance, detail CV, focal contrast ratios, k-means palette, colourfulness) turn vague critique into reference deltas, but are not absolute aesthetic scores.
keyFindings.detail: Hasler-Susstrunk colourfulness (~15 slightly, ~82 highly, ~109 extremely colourful) has no linear relation to aesthetics overall. Spectral-residual saliency at 64 px is crude (it found the window, not the kin).
keyFindings.implicationForOrbkin: Use artcheck.py (in the notes, verified in this container) to compute deltas against the reference crops and between iterations, and feed the notan/squint images to the VLM critic.

techniques.name: Rubric-driven screenshot critique with located evidence
techniques.why: Turns a 6/10 vibe into specific, ranked fixes, and stops a VLM from rubber-stamping
techniques.how: 15-item rubric (art-direction.md section 2), 0-2 each with image-located evidence, derived images first, side-by-side with the reference, top-3 deltas ranked
techniques.effort: low: a skill file plus the script

techniques.name: Subject/ground separation (complementary floor patch + rim light + selective outline)
techniques.why: The creatures currently share value and hue with their ground
techniques.how: Desaturated complementary or neutral tone in the floor area under the kin, a rim term in the sprite toon shader for warm-on-warm pairings, and an outline colour from a darkened adjacent ramp

techniques.name: Detail falloff (light- and focus-modulated texture detail)
techniques.why: Uniform noise kills focal hierarchy (meadow detail CV 0.20)
techniques.how: Painters take a detail parameter: lit faces near the focus get cracks and chips, shadow and far faces get 2-3 flat shades. Bake per block from the light direction and distance to the battle spots

techniques.name: Per-arena gamut and reserved accent hues
techniques.why: Prevents the monochrome scene and guarantees kin and UI pop
techniques.how: An arena palette file (allowed ramps + reserved hues); a unit test samples painter outputs; the grade pushes shadows cool

techniques.name: Light-shaft discipline
techniques.why: Shafts are currently the brightest mass and wash out the kin
techniques.how: 2-3 shafts with a visible source, landing beside the kin; additive light on the kin region capped at about +8 L*

techniques.name: Foreground framing plane
techniques.why: Dioramas read as a window into a world when the edges are dark and near-silhouette
techniques.how: A dark rock lip or overhang or foliage in the bottom corners, lit only by fill

techniques.name: World-cohesive pixel UI
techniques.why: The UI is currently the most off-style, saturated element
techniques.how: Nine-slice pixel frames at the world texel scale, cream/ink palette from the arena, pixel typeface at integer scale, colour only for state and focus

techniques.name: Silhouette and lineup tests
techniques.why: Shape language and distinctness are a designer's first read
techniques.how: Render black silhouettes at 32/64 px; compute solidity and pairwise IoU; flag IoU > 0.8 and blobby high-solidity builds

techniques.name: VFX primary/secondary audit
techniques.why: Riot's guide is the industry reference for readable FX
techniques.how: Per move: one opaque, high-value primary shape; soft secondaries; anticipation-climax-dissipation; scale equals power
